column1: 爾時， 心王菩薩聞佛說法， 出三界外不可思議，
column2: At that time Simwang Bodhisattva heard the Buddha's explanation of the dharma, which transcended the three realms of existence and was inconceivable.

column1: 從座而起， 叉手合掌， 以偈問曰： 「如來所說義， 出世無有相。
column2: Arising from his seat he joined his palms together in supplication and asked in gāthās: The meaning of what the Tathāgata has said, Transcends the world and is free from characteristics, It enables all sentient beings, To complete the annihilation of the outflows.

column1: 可有一切生， 皆得盡有漏？ 斷結空心我， 是則無有生。
column2: Eradicating the bonds and emptying both mind and self, This then will be [the state of] nonproduction.

column1: 云何無有生， 而得無生忍？
column2: But how will one gain the acceptance of the nonproduction [of dharmas], If there is nothing that is produced?

column1: 」爾時， 佛告心王菩薩言： 「善男子！
column2: At that time, the Buddha proclaimed to Simwang Bodhisattva: "Oh son of good family!

column1: 無生法忍法本無生， 諸行無生非無生行，
column2: The acceptance of the nonproduction of dharmas [means to realize that] dharmas are originally unproduced and that all practices produce nothing.

column1: 得無生忍即為虛妄。
column2: As there is no way to practice this nonproduction, achieving the acceptance of nonproduction is in fact a deception."

column1: 」心王菩薩言：
column2: Simwang Bodhisattva asked, "Lord!

column1: 「尊者！ 得無生忍即為虛妄？ 無得無忍應非虛妄！
column2: You say that 'achieving the acceptance of nonproduction is in fact a deception.' [But is the converse then true: that] nonachievement and nonacceptance perforce are not deceptions?"

column1: 」佛言：
column2: The Buddha replied, "Not so.

column1: 「不也。 何以故？
column2: Why is this?

column1: 無得無忍是則有得，
column2: If nonachievement and nonacceptance exist, then so would achievement.

column1: 有得有忍是則有生。
column2: If achievement and acceptance exist, then so would production.

column1: 有生於得， 有所得法，
column2: If achievement is produced, there then would exist dharmas that are the objects of that achievement.

column1: 並為虛妄。
column2: So both [achievement and acceptance] are deceptions."

column1: 」心王菩薩言：
column2: Simwang Bodhisattva asked, "Lord!

column1: 「尊者！ 云何無忍無生心而非虛妄？
column2: How is it that the mind may be free from either acceptance or production and yet not be deceived?"

column1: 」佛言： 「無忍無生心者， 心無形段，
column2: The Buddha replied, "The mind that is free from both acceptance and production—that mind has neither form nor shape.

column1: 猶如火性，
column2: It is like heat [lit.

column2: the nature of fire], which, though latent in wood, cannot be found there.

column1: 決定性故。
column2: This is because the nature [of the mind] is fixed.

column1: 但名、但字， 性不可得，
column2: [Mind] is nothing more than a name and a word; its nature is unascertainable.

column1: 欲詮其理假說為名， 名不可得；
column2: Wishing to allude to this principle, [the buddhas] have provisionally named it [mind], but this name is unascertainable.

column1: 心相亦爾， 不見處所，
column2: This is also the case for the characteristics of the mind: their location cannot be found.

column1: 知心如是， 則無生心。
column2: If one knows that the mind is like this, the mind will then not produce anything.

column1: 「善男子！
column2:
Oh son of good family!
是心性相又如阿摩勒果， 本不自生、不從他生， 不共生、不因生、不無生。	The nature and characteristics of the mind are like the āmalaka (myrobalan) fruit: they are not self-generated; they are not generated by some external agent; they are not produced in conjunction with something else; they are not produced in the absence of a cause for that production.
何以故？	Why is this?
緣代謝故。	Because these conditions [of production and extinction] alternate successively.
緣起非生、緣謝非滅，	These conditions are generated, but there is no production; these conditions decay, but there is no extinction.
隱顯無相，	Whether hidden or made manifest, [nature and characteristics] are signless.
根理寂滅。	Their fundamental principle is calm and extinct.
在無有處， 不見所住， 決定性故。	There is no place where they abide, nor is there seen anything that abides, because their natures are fixed.
是決定性， 亦不一、不異， 不斷、不常， 不入、不出， 不生、不滅，	This fixed nature is neither unitary nor different; neither evanescent nor permanent; it has neither access nor egress and is neither produced nor extinguished.

column1: 離諸四謗言語道斷；
column2: It abandons all four of these alternatives (cakuṣkoṭi), for the pathways of words and speech are eradicated (ǒnǒdodan) .

column1: 無生心性亦復如是。 云何說生不生、有忍無忍？
column2: This is the case as well for the unproduced nature of the mind: how can it be said that it is either produced or unproduced, either accepted or not accepted?

column1: 若有說心有得、有住及以見者， 即為不得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。
column2:
If a person claims that the mind may either achieve [something] or abide [somewhere] and takes this as his [wrong] view, then he will not attain anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi [complete, perfect enlightenment] and prajna.
般若是為長夜了別心性者，	This is the 'long night' [of saṃsāra].
知心性如是； 性亦如是，	One who has comprehended the mind-nature knows that the mind-nature is thus and that the nature is also thus.
無生、無行。	This is the practice of nonproduction.

column1: 」心王菩薩言：
column2: Simwang Bodhisattva commented, "Lord!

column1: 「尊者！ 心若本如無生於行，
column2: As the mind is originally thus, it will not produce such practices.

column1: 諸行無生。 生行不生， 不生無行，
column2: As all practices are unproduced, there will be no practice that produces anything and this nonproduction will then not need to be practiced.

column1: 即無生行也。
column2: This in fact is the practice of nonproduction."

column1: 」佛言： 「善男子！
column2: The Buddha asked, "Oh son of good family!

column1: 汝以無生而證無生行也？
column2: Can you realize the practice of nonproduction by not producing anything?"

column1: 」心王菩薩言： 「不也。
column2: Simwang Bodhisattva replied, "No.

column1: 何以故？
column2: And why is this?

column1: 如無生行， 性相空寂，
column2: In the actual practice of nonproduction, both nature and characteristics are void and calm.

column1: 無見、無聞， 無得、無失， 無言、無說，
column2: There is neither vision nor hearing; neither gain nor loss; neither words nor speech; neither cognition nor characteristics; neither clinging nor rejection.

column1: 無知、無相， 無取、無捨， 云何取證？
column2: So how could one cling to this realization?

column1: 若取證者， 即為諍論。
column2: If one clings to this realization, this would in fact serve [as the cause of] disputation and contention.

column1: 無諍、無論， 乃無生行。
column2: Only when there is neither disputation nor contention is it the practice of nonproduction."

column1: 」佛言： 「汝得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提也。
column2: The Buddha said, "Have you attained anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi?” Simwang Bodhisattva responded, "Lord!

column1: 」心王菩薩言： 「尊者！ 我無得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。
column2: I am free from any attainment of anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi.

column1: 何以故？
column2: And why is this?

column1: 菩提性中無得、無失， 無覺、無知， 無分別相，
column2: The bodhi-nature has neither gain nor loss, neither attention nor cognition, for it is free from all differentiated characteristics.

column1: 無分別中即清淨性。
column2: The pure nature actually exists in such nondiscrimination.

column1: 性無間雜， 無有言說， 非有、非無， 非知、非不知；
column2: This nature is free from any extraneous admixture [such as the dichotomies of production and extinction or subject and object]: it is free from words and speech; it neither exists nor does not exist; it is neither aware nor nescient.

column1: 諸可法行亦復如是。
column2:
So too is this case for all the dharmas [training methods] that can be cultivated.
何以故？	Why is this?
一切法行， 不見處所， 決定性故。	All dharmas and practices have no loci that can be found, because their natures are fixed.
本無有得、不得，	Originally, they are free from any semblance of attainment or nonattainment.
云何得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提？ 」佛言：	So how can one attain anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhil The Buddha replied, "So it is, so it is.

column1: 「如是， 如是。 如汝所言， 一切心行， 不過無相體寂無生，
column2: As you have said, all of the activities of mind are nothing but signlessness; their essences are calm and unproduced.

column1: 可有諸識亦復如是。
column2: It is the same as well with each and every consciousness.

column1: 何以故？
column2: Why is this?

column1: 眼、眼觸悉皆空寂，
column2: The eye and visual contact are both void and calm.

column1: 識亦空寂， 無有動、不動相，
column2: [Visual] consciousness is also void and calm: it is free from any characteristic of agitation or motionlessness.

column1: 內無三受， 三受寂滅；
column2: Since it is free internally of the three feelings [vedanā; pain, pleasure, and neutral feeling], the three feelings are calm and extinct.

column1: 耳、鼻、舌、身、心意意識， 及以末那、阿梨耶識亦復如是， 皆亦不生寂滅之心及無生心。
column2: So too is this the case for auditory, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, and mental [consciousnesses], as well as mind-consciousness, mano[vijñāna], and alaya consciousness: as all of them are also unproduced, they are the mind that is calm and extinct and the mind that produces nothing.

column1: 若生寂滅心、若生無生心， 是有生行， 非無生行。
column2: But if one gives rise to the mind that is calm and extinct and the mind that produces nothing, this then would be practice that produces something, not the practice of nonproduction.

column1: 菩薩內生三受、三行、三戒，
column2:
Bodhisattva! Thus internally are generated three feelings, three karmic actions, and three moral restraints [of physical, verbal, and mental actions].
若已寂滅， 生心不生。 心常寂滅， 無功、無用，	If these are already calm and extinct, the producing mind will not be produced and the mind will be constantly calm and extinct, without efficacy or function.
不證寂滅相， 亦不住於無證，	He does not evince any characteristic of calm extinction; but he also does not insist on not corroborating [such a characteristic].
可處無住總持無相，	What is worth lingering in is the state of nonabiding, wherein is encoded (ch'ongji, dhārayati) signlessness.
則無三受、三行、三戒， 悉皆寂滅清淨無住，	Then, there will be none of these three, such as the three feelings, and so forth, for all will be calm and extinct, pure and nonabiding.
不入三昧、不住坐禪，	He need not access samādhi; he need not persist in sitting in dhyāna.
無生、無行。	This is nonproduction and freedom from practice.

column1: 」心王菩薩言： 「禪能攝動， 定諸幻亂。
column2: Simwang Bodhisattva asked, "Dhyāna can suppress all agitation and allay all illusory distractions.

column1: 云何不禪？
column2: Why this negation of dhyāna?"

column1: 」佛言：
column2: The Buddha replied, "Bodhisattva!

column1: 「菩薩禪即是動，
column2: Dhyāna in fact is agitation.

column1: 不動、不禪是無生禪。
column2: Being neither agitated nor concentrated is the dhyana that produces nothing.

column1: 禪性無生， 離生禪相；
column2: The nature of dhyana is to produce nothing; it has no characteristics of the dhyana that does produce something.

column1: 禪性無住， 離住禪動。
column2: The nature of dhyāna is to linger nowhere; it leaves far behind the agitation caused by trying to linger in dhyāna.

column1: 若知禪性無有動靜， 即得無生；
column2: Know that the nature of dhyāna is free from both agitation and calmness and you will immediately attain the [acceptance of the] nonproduction [of dharmas] and the prajñā that produces nothing.

column1: 無生般若亦不依住，
column2: But also do not rely on, or linger over, these.

column1: 心亦不動； 以是智故，
column2: Because of this knowledge, the mind also will not be agitated.

column1: 故得無生般若波羅蜜。
column2: For this reason, you will attain the prajñāpāramitā that produces nothing."

column1: 」心王菩薩言：
column2: Simwang Bodhisattva said, "Lord!

column1: 「尊者！ 無生般若於一切處無住， 於一切處無離，
column2: The prajñā that produces nothing does not abide anywhere, and yet there is no place where it is not.

column1: 心無住處， 無處住心，
column2: The mind has no abiding place and there is no place where the mind can abide.

column1: 無住無心， 心無生住。
column2: When there is no abiding and no mind (musim), the mind will then abide in nonproduction.

column1: 如此住心， 即無生住。
column2: The mind that so abides is in fact abiding in nonproduction.

column1: 尊者！
column2:
Lord!
心無生住不可思議！	The mind's practice of nonproduction is inconceivable.
不思議中可不可說！	As it is inconceivable, it is both effable and ineffable.

column1: 」佛言： 「如是， 如是。
column2: The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is."

column1: 」心王菩薩聞如是言， 歎未曾有， 而說偈言： 「滿足大智尊， 廣說無生法，
column2: Simwang Bodhisattva heard these words and, praising its miraculousness, recited these gāthās: That Lord who is replete in great knowledge, Has explained extensively the dharma of nonproduction.

column1: 聞所未曾聞， 未說而今說。
column2: I have heard what has never been heard before, Now has been explained what had yet to be explained.

column1: 猶如淨甘露， 時時乃一出， 難遇難思議，
column2: Like the pure sweet dew, That appears but once in a long while, [So too is this dharma] difficult to encounter and difficult to imagine.

column1: 聞者亦復難。 無上良福田、  最上勝妙藥，
column2: Difficult too is it to hear it, It is the unsurpassed, excellent field of merit (puṇyakṣetra), The supremely efficacious, sublime medicine.

column1: 為度眾生故， 而今為宣說。
column2: It is in order to ferry across sentient beings, That it has now been proclaimed.

column1: 」爾時， 眾中聞說此已， 皆得無生無生般若。
column2: At that time, all those in the congregation heard these words and attained the [acceptance of] the nonproduction [of dharmas] as well as the prajñā that produces nothing.
